decisions.reason: As a broad adjacent supplement line with several variants, it remains a relatively low-cost consumer-health option for an expanding pharmaceutical firm, so despite limited recent website evidence it is still more likely to be retained than abandoned.

This hair-and-skin supplement sits close to the firm's pharmacy-based consumer-health business and is inexpensive to carry, but after several years in a crowded category the option value is lower and pruning risk is meaningful.

Joint-health supplements fit the firm's established adjacent offer and likely have a stable pharmacy customer base, so the product is still worth keeping unless clearer negative sales evidence emerges.

Because this mushroom-based immune supplement is a narrower and more fad-sensitive niche, the years since launch likely revealed enough about limited upside that the firm would now reallocate resources elsewhere.

The earlier Valsartan-related quality and regulatory problem is a strong negative signal in a sensitive generic prescription category, so real-options logic favors abandoning this product rather than continuing to bear compliance and reputational risk.

The OTC migraine triptan is newer than the 2018 launches and offers potentially attractive strategic value in consumer health, so with uncertainty still not fully resolved it is worth keeping on the market for now.
